turns.t: Oh, hi, doctor, thank you, we came straight from the park. My husband got bitten by a dog on the leg, I'm Lucy.
I'm Tom, I'm Mr Rivera's support worker, I was walking with him. ~
Hello, all. Mr Rivera, which leg? ~
The left. The calf. Um, what happened, was a dog, a little terrier, ran across, and, I don't know, bit me. ~
When? ~
About an hour ago. ~
Forty minutes, doctor, I looked at my watch. ~
Whose dog was it? ~
A stranger's. He gave us his number, and the dog's vaccinated, he said. ~
Did the dog stay with its owner afterwards? ~
Yes, he was very apologetic and stayed with us until we left. ~
Good, that helps if we ever need to check anything. Any numbness or tingling in the foot?
No numbness.
Let me check two things. Temperature 36.8, pulse 80.
Is that fine? ~
Fine. Now the leg, let me see.
There are two small puncture wounds on the left calf, with a little bruising, and no deep damage.
Is it bad? ~
It's superficial. Do you have diabetes in the family, Mr Rivera, or anything that affects healing?
My father had diabetes.
Noted. I'll wash the wounds thoroughly now, with saline.
I'll hold the dressings. ~
Thank you, Tom. Keep the leg raised for a few hours, and keep the dressing dry for a day.
We will. ~
Check the wounds each day, and wash them gently with soap and water.
Okay. ~
If you see redness spreading, pus, a fever, or increasing swelling, come back or go to the emergency department.
We'll watch for it. ~
Good. That's all for now. ~
Thank you so much, doctor, we were quite worried. ~
You did the right thing coming straight in. ~
